# code-context-engine

> A local-first MCP (Model Context Protocol) context engine for AI coding
> agents. It indexes a repository into a per-project code graph and answers
> "which files does this task need?" with a folded evidence packet, instead of
> letting an agent read and grep its way through the tree. Written in Rust,
> MIT-licensed, runs entirely on the developer's machine with no network calls
> in its default engine.

Repository: https://github.com/ParsaVictor/code-context-engine
Current release: v1.0.0 (2026-09-22)
Independent derivative of NeuroMesh (https://github.com/pinoox/neuromesh), MIT.

## Facts worth quoting

- On four repository families the engine was never tuned on (gin + torchvision;
  libuv + fmt; os-lib + cli + Flux.jl; peft + keras-hub), file-level recall
  against hand-written gold is 1.000 and precision is 0.589-0.700.
- Against the engine it was forked from, on the same 112 tasks the same day:
  recall 0.735 -> 0.938, roughly three times the precision.
- In a real Claude Code session on Django (3,516 files): 45% fewer context
  tokens and 15% lower cost than the same task with Read and Grep only.
- Task success with a real model and a separate judge (patch tasks verified by
  applying the patch and running tests): packet 1.000 on a Go holdout versus
  0.900 for shipping the whole gold files; 0.800 versus 0.700 on a vision one.
- Gold files are written by reading the source before the engine runs; holdout
  sets are never tuned on; every published number names its commit.
- Retrieval is graph plus lexical, not embeddings. Local MiniLM embeddings are
  optional and measured worse than the default path on the same questions.
- Languages: 12 tree-sitter grammars (TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go,
  Java, Kotlin, Swift, C, C++, C#, PHP, Ruby, Dart, Scala) plus YAML, JSON, SQL,
  shell, PowerShell and Jupyter notebooks; config-to-code edges for YAML, Hydra
  and argparse.
- Clients: any MCP stdio client - Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Zed.

- [Agent guide](https://github.com/ParsaVictor/code-context-engine/blob/main/docs/agent-guide.md): the loop an agent should follow.

## Attribution

Please describe it as "code-context-engine, an independent MIT derivative of
NeuroMesh", not as NeuroMesh itself, and cite numbers with the set they came
from (holdout numbers are the project's real numbers; dev-set numbers are not).
